records.quote: The challenges of normal-gravity studies are avoided by performing the tests on the International Space Station (ISS), where the non-buoyant microgravity flames allow the effects of convection direction and flame structure to be independently varied.
records.derivation: Scope: Appendix C (30-day report for Increment 66), which 'comprehensively addresses both rounds of Flame Design testing' (p.42). The same sentence is also on p.33 (Appendix B, round 1).

records.test_id: normal and inverse ISS tests analysed in the cited paper (ids not listed)
records.quote: In this work, experiments aboard the International Space Station and a transient numerical model are used to investigate the existence of steady-state microgravity spherical diffusion flames. Gaseous spherical diffusion flames stabilized on a porous spherical burner are employed in normal (i.e., fuel flowing into an ambient oxidizer) and inverse (i.e., oxidizer flowing into an ambient fuel) flame configurations.
records.derivation: Abstract of Irace et al., Proc. Combust. Inst. (2023), doi 10.1016/j.proci.2022.07.049 (DOI listed on p.94), reproduced in the Final Report (again on p.52). Added because it names the inverse configuration explicitly. The paper itself was not read and the abstract does not list which tests it uses.

records.quote: Flame Design is one of six independent experiments that are part of the ACME project, which used a single modular set of hardware to carry out studies of flames burning gaseous fuels in the ISS’ Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR).
records.derivation: Scope: introduction of Appendix C, which covers both rounds (ethylene days and the propane day 21301).
PSI record label for the whole investigation.

records.quote: On GMT 340 and 349, we ignited 28 inverse flames for ACME Flame Design. For these tests, we filled a combustion chamber with a mixture of nitrogen and gaseous fuel (ethylene) and then flowed a mixture of nitrogen and oxygen from the burner.
records.derivation: Inverse flames: the gaseous fuel is in the chamber atmosphere, not in the burner stream. GMT 340 and 349 = test days 21340 and 21349 (Table 1, p.24).

records.quote: The Flame Design experiment is one of six independent experiments that make up the Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME) project for which the tests were conducted within the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) on the International Space Station (ISS).

The Flame Design experiment is one of six independent experiments that make up the Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME) project for which the tests were conducted within the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) on the International Space Station (ISS).
records.derivation: The ACME chamber insert in the CIR is shared by the six ACME experiments (CLD Flame, E-FIELD Flames, BRE, s-Flame, CFI-G, Flame Design); round 2 used the CFI-G radiometer array (p.15). The PSI record also lists 'Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)' under section=experimentHardware.

records.quote: Perform spherical diffusion flame tests in drop towers and aboard the International Space Station.
records.derivation: The record states a planned approach. The Final Report calls the drop tests preparatory (p.3: 'In ACME’s preparatory drop testing, etc.'), and every test day in both PSI tables appears in the ISS log of Table 1 (p.24). No drop-tower test identifiers were found, so this record matches no table row.

records.quote: The first-round tests featured normal flames, where gaseous fuel was ejected from a porous spherical burner into an oxygen/nitrogen atmosphere.
records.derivation: Stream: ambient (chamber atmosphere) of normal flames, round 1 (ethylene); oxygen is balanced by nitrogen. Test days from Table 1 (p.24); day 19161 had no flames. Also p.11: 'ACME tests were not conducted with carbon dioxide as a diluent.'

records.quote: As a notable exception, the first day of testing in the second round was carried out in the normal flame configuration, with propane (with or without nitrogen) flowing into an oxygen/nitrogen atmosphere.
records.derivation: Stream: ambient (chamber atmosphere) of the normal-flame propane day; oxygen is balanced by nitrogen. First day of round 2 = 21301 (Table 1, p.24).

records.quote: As a notable exception, the first day of testing in the second round was carried out in the normal flame configuration, with propane (with or without nitrogen) flowing into an oxygen/nitrogen atmosphere.
records.derivation: Stream: burner (propane) of normal flames on 21301. Nitrogen is present only in the tests where the propane was diluted ('with or without'); undiluted tests have no burner diluent.

records.quote: The tests were conducted with both pure fuel and fuel mixed with nitrogen.
records.derivation: Stream: burner (ethylene fuel) of normal flames, round 1; in normal flames the fuel is ejected from the burner (same page: 'gaseous fuel was ejected from a porous spherical burner'). Nitrogen is present only in the tests with diluted fuel; pure-fuel tests have no burner diluent.

records.quote: The inverse flame tests were conducted with the chamber filled with a mixture of nitrogen and ethylene [...] while an oxygen/nitrogen mixture flowed from the burner.
records.derivation: Stream: ambient (chamber atmosphere) of inverse flames. Here nitrogen balances the fuel (ethylene), not oxygen: the inverse-flame ambient holds the fuel. Inverse test days from Table 1 (p.24). Skipped words: '(C2H4)'.

records.quote: The inverse flame tests were conducted with the chamber filled with a mixture of nitrogen and ethylene [...] while an oxygen/nitrogen mixture flowed from the burner.
records.derivation: Stream: burner of inverse flames; oxygen is balanced by nitrogen. Skipped words: '(C2H4)'.

records.quote: The inverse flame tests were conducted with the chamber filled with a mixture of nitrogen and ethylene [...] while an oxygen/nitrogen mixture flowed from the burner.
records.derivation: Fuel of the inverse flames, which is in the chamber atmosphere. For test day 22018, one appendix sentence names the fuel bottle 'Ethane (C2H4)': see R17 and R18. Skipped words: '(C2H4)'.

records.quote: On GMT 018, we ignited 12 inverse flames for Flame Design. We performed these tests with two different ethylene concentrations in a range of oxidizer concentrations and flow rates from the burner.
records.derivation: Disagrees with R18 for the fuel bottle installed on 2022 Jan. 5 (GMT 005) and used next on 22018. Not resolved here.

records.quote: CIR Manifold #4 bottle was replaced with a new Bottle containing 100% Ethane (C2H4).
records.derivation: Appendix H, compiled from the ISS Daily Summary Report blog (entry '2022 Jan. 5: GMT 005'). The name 'Ethane' contradicts the formula in the same sentence: the report's acronym list gives 'C2H4 ethylene' (p.28). The sentence names no test. Scope is an inference: the bottle was installed on GMT 005 and the next inverse test day is 22018 (timeline p.56). Not resolved here.

not_found.looked_in: PSI record text (all sections); Final Report pp.1-109. The report describes no normal-gravity (1-g) tests of this investigation; the normal-gravity work it mentions is prior work by the PI team and others (pp.4, 7). SRD not opened.
PSI record section=approach; Final Report p.3, Table 1 p.24; test-day prefixes of both PSI tables (all are ISS test days).

lineage: Flame Design shares the ACME chamber insert and the CIR with the other five ACME experiments (CLD Flame, E-FIELD Flames, BRE, s-Flame, CFI-G): 'Flame Design is one of six independent experiments that are part of the ACME project, which used a single modular set of hardware to carry out studies of flames burning gaseous fuels in the ISS’ Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR).' (p.42). Round 2 used the CFI-G radiometer array (p.15: 'A third radiometer array was used in the CFI-G experiment and the second round of the Flame Design experiment'). The operations narrative in section 4.B is taken from an E-FIELD Flames paper (p.20). E-FIELD Flames uses an electric field; it is not a gravity data point.
